correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the forbidden-subgraph condition: a face of size at least four must have all but at most one vertex in one part, otherwise part-patterns i,j,i,j or i,j,i,k or i,j,k,l make a four-vertex path. For each owner part i, toggling a distinguished owner vertex x_i pairs every face of size >=4; in an alternating path, the next deletion keeps x_i and at least two owner vertices, so that face is never another lower match. Hence the matching is acyclic and leaves only dimensions 0,1,2. The full two-skeleton gives simple connectivity; a simply connected two-dimensional CW model is a wedge of beta_2 spheres by Hurewicz/Whitehead. Counting unmatched owner-triangles yields exactly B. Independently enumerated forbidden paths and all faces and checked reduced Euler rank for (1,1),(2,3),(2,2,2),(1,2,3),(3,3,3),(1,1,2,2),(2,2,2,2): ranks 0,2,10,7,38,10,35 respectively. These finite instances corroborate rather than establish the uniform theorem.

final_claim: For every r>=2 and positive part sizes n_i, the four-vertex subgraph-path-free complex PF_4(K_{n_1,...,n_r}) is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of B two-spheres, B=C(N-1,3)-sum_i[C(n_i-1,3)+(N-n_i) C(n_i-1,2)], N=sum_i n_i. Zero spheres means contractible; holds for singleton parts. The r=2 case is acknowledged as already known.
